headline: ASK demands impartial probe into journalist's killing in Netrokona
summary: Human rights organization Ain and Salish Kendra (ASK) has called for the immediate identification and prosecution of those responsible for the murder of Lutfuzzaman Alif Fakir.
details: Lutfuzzaman Alif Fakir, the Netrokona representative for the private IPTV channel Ruposhi Bangla, was shot dead in the Telanjia area of Durgapur on October 15.
The human rights organization Ain and Salish Kendra (ASK) has expressed deep concern and strong condemnation over the killing, demanding a fair and effective investigation.
ASK highlighted that Alif Fakir had previously been attacked in November 2025, and the failure to ensure his safety after that incident is highly concerning.
The organization stated that the killing of a journalist is not just an attack on one life, but a dangerous signal for independent journalism, freedom of expression, and the public's right to know.

ASK noted that the right to life and freedom of the press are guaranteed under Articles 32 and 39 of the Bangladesh Constitution, as well as the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR).
Executive Director of ASK, Tahmina Rahman, emphasized that there should be no negligence, influence, or bias in the investigation of this murder.
The organization called on authorities to ensure a safe environment where journalists can perform their professional duties without fear of threats or insecurity.
caption:
A journalist was shot dead in Netrokona, and now human rights activists are demanding justice. Why was he not protected after a previous attack?

headline_marked: 90 deaths in 16 days: [[Dengue turns deadlier in October]]
headline: 90 deaths in 16 days: Dengue turns deadlier in October
summary: Over 28,000 people were hospitalised in the first half of October as health experts warn of delayed diagnosis and treatment complications.
details: At least 90 dengue patients died and 28,820 were hospitalised in the first 16 days of October, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The death toll has risen sharply compared to previous months, with 148 deaths in September, 43 in August, and 36 in July.
A review by the Institute of Epidemiology, Disease Control and Research found that more than one-third of reviewed patients died within a single day of hospital admission.
Experts attribute the rising deaths to delayed hospitalisation, inadequate early diagnosis, and the absence of an effective three-tier management system.

Medicine specialist Dr ABM Abdullah warned that repeated infections can lead to severe complications, increasing the risk of death, especially for children and those with underlying health conditions.
Prof HM Nazmul Ahsan noted inconsistent application of national treatment guidelines, warning that unnecessary platelet transfusions or inappropriate fluid loading can contribute to death.
Public health expert Mushtuq Husain suggested a three-tier management system to reduce pressure on major hospitals by providing initial testing at primary healthcare facilities.
Entomologist Prof Kabirul Bashar predicts that while cases might decline slightly in November, a significant drop is unlikely before December.
